lines: Brackwater. Forty boats, two of them working.
Not for want of crew. For want of a channel worth taking a boat down.
Mabry is out on the pier. She has been out on the pier since Tuesday.
She gave you the Seal. Then I will tell you what I told her.
The Concord took soundings off my pier for six weeks. Always after dark.
A survey is a survey. But an honest one does not need the dark.

bw_netter: Flats are heaving. Everything that lives in deep water has come up onto the mud.
That is not a good year. That is a run.
bw_child: Dad says the sea is holding its breath.
I asked what happens when it lets go.
He did not answer, so I asked louder, and he still did not answer.
bw_greeter: Waystation west, provisioner east, Bastion at the end of the pier.
Mind the lanes either side of the hall. The middle is deep and it does not forgive.

lines: No, I cannot tell you the numbers. No, that is not sinister.
You spoke to the Director. Then you have heard it properly and I need not perform.
I will tell you the part she leaves out because it is not persuasive.
We do not know what happens to everything that migrates once the current stops.
We have models. The models disagree with each other.

bw_sailor: Sixty years I read this channel. Currents, colour, the way the birds sit.
Now it is flat as a table and I cannot read a table.
A flat sea is not a calm sea, lad. A flat sea is a held one.
bw_house: My husband fished the deep channel. Thirty-one years.
He went out in the spring and the water did not move the boat. Not once, all day.
He came home and sat down and did not go out again.
He is not frightened of storms. He is frightened of stillness. So am I.
